state.audience: older adults 60+, preventive or mild cognitive decline, some age-related hearing loss
state.app: warm bilingual cognitive mini-games, non-clinical, offline-first, zero third-party dependencies
state.constraints: sounds must be free to use with no licensing fees; haptics available
state.events: correct answer, incorrect answer, round start, game completion

positive_net.instructions: For this audience, is well-chosen sound a net positive (engagement, feedback clarity) rather than a net negative (confusion, irritation)?

criteria.true: Gentle, meaningful, easy to switch off
criteria.false: Risk of startling or confusing the player

soft_low_tones.instructions: Are short, soft, low-frequency success tones more appropriate than sharp high-pitched beeps for older adults, including those with mild hearing loss?

criteria.true: Lower frequencies carry better for age-related hearing loss

custom_vs_system.instructions: Should we synthesize warm custom tones rather than use stock iOS system alert sounds?

criteria.true: Custom tones match the warm, non-clinical brand
criteria.false: System sounds are familiar and expected

fewer_distinct.instructions: Should the sound palette stay small (three or fewer distinct sounds) to avoid confusing this audience?

criteria.true: Fewer, consistent sounds are easier to learn

opt_in_default.instructions: Should sound be ON by default with an easy off switch, rather than opt-in?

criteria.true: Feedback helps most players out of the box
criteria.false: Sound should be opt-in to avoid startling

redundant_cues.instructions: Must every sound have a visual and haptic counterpart so nothing relies on sound alone?

criteria.false: Sound can be the only cue for some events
